text:
carmen: Heads-up — canary perf test (mini-batch=auto) shows host-side CPU rising ~3x for short streams. Profiling attached, need eyes. TL;DR: parse/tokenize + grpc writev spikes.

ashok: looking. which branch?

carmen: host-opt/batching-hints (deployed to canary), test script: `loadtest --streams 5k`

nina: quick note — KV-cache eviction rate jumped in that run, maybe small payloads thrash shards.

tom: saw similar yesterday; my perf top shows syscalls in writev + memcpy in ingress parser. paste:

```bash
# perf top snippet
 12.3%  libc-2.31.so  [.] writev
  8.7%  host_ingress   [.] parse_frame
  6.1%  host_tokenizer [.] tokenize_single
```

ashok: interesting — batching_hints changed kernel select path? maybe shorter sequences force different kernel leading to extra CPU.

carmen: yes kernel selector pr #482 toggles small-seq path. If batch sizes <=4 it picks scalar kernels causing per-token overhead.

nina: Also KV cache metric: kvcache.local_evictions/sec spiked from 2 to 220. Might be because fragmenting streams produce many tiny prefixes.

tom: Temp mitigation — reduced autonomous min-batch to 8 and disabled kv-prefetch, reran, CPU back down ~40%.

jen: Can we get a binary diff of the kernel selector? Also add telemetry for batch_size distribution and seq_len histogram.

carmen: adding metrics: route.batch_size_p50,p95; route.seq_len_p50,p95; kvcache.hit_rate. Also adding a tracing span around tokenizer and parse.

ashok: for short term, revert the selector tweak in canary and run canary2 with bigger min-batch.

infra-bot: deploy rollback scheduled @ 3323456795 by ashok — canary group host-opt/batching-hints -> previous commit

tom: after rollback, CPU stable. Need follow-up: improve batching heuristics to prefer kernel-friendly batch grouping for short seqs; and coalesce writes to reduce writev calls.

nina: also exploring tokenization pipeline: pool of tokenizers with batching interface to avoid per-request allocs. prototype: `token_pool.acquire().batch_tokenize(reqs)`

carmen: opened follow-up issues: INF-921 batching heuristics; INF-922 tokenizer pooling; INF-923 kvcache shard smoothing.

jen: nice. Can someone own INF-921? ashok?

ashok: I'll take INF-921. ETA EOD tomorrow for a spike.

carmen: thanks, will post perf numbers once spike done. Link to perf trace: https://perf.example/trace/3323456789

tom: :eyes:
